statement: The input moves lists [from, to] moves of a game; a player who cannot move loses. A position is won when some move leads to a lost position, lost when every move leads to a won one, and drawn otherwise, as the well-founded semantics of the rule win(x) :- move(x, y), not win(y) says. The program's value is a record {"won", "lost", "drawn"} of the positions in each, each list in ascending order.
origin: The win-move game, the standard example of the well-founded semantics (Van Gelder, Ross, and Schlipf, 1991)
